findings.finding: First record uses exclusive creation; each buffered append checks byte count, flushes and fsyncs before pointer update. First directory entry is fsynced.

A copied snapshot omits only inline cleanup for intermediate checkpoints. Existing temporary write, file fsync, replace and directory fsync remain. Prefix metadata identifies committed bytes, SHA256 and record count.

Crash or exception before pointer update leaves preceding committed prefix authoritative. A trailing partial or complete unreferenced record is not evidence of successful completion. Missing pointer denotes no committed records, not no children.

Normal final checkpoint includes original full inline array plus storage metadata. Append/fsync failure propagates into failed status. Inline final records may exceed last committed prefix. Finalizer catches cleanup journaling errors and retains failure. Divergence is permitted only on failed terminal records; a passed receipt must agree with its full prefix.
